messages.subject_clean: reciprocal overlap of reads and genomic feature
messages.body_plain:
Am I correct that subread does not have option for reciprocal overlap as coverage or multicov in BEDtools do:
"-r Require that the fraction of overlap be reciprocal for A and B. In other words, if -f is 0.90 and -r is used, this requires that B overlap at least 90% of A and that A also overlaps at least 90% of B."
Option −−fracOverlap is not reciprocal.

It would be for my very beneficial to add this option.

Hannes Luidalepp

messages.subject: Segmentation fault with subjunc
messages.body_plain:
Dear Subread Support Team,

I recently ran the subjunc aligner over a RNA-Seq sample from GSE46876 in Ubuntu, but got the "segmentation fault" error message. Please see the following details to reproduce this issue:

1. Download the RNA-Seq sampel from ftp://ftp-trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sra/sra-instant/reads/ByExp/sra/SRX/SRX307/SRX307023/SRR902884/SRR902884.sra
2. Convert the data from SRA to FASTQ using the following command line:
    sratoolkit.2.3.5-2-ubuntu64/bin/fastq-dump --split-3 SRR902884.sra
    This will generate SRR902884.fastq
3. Run the subjunc aligner:

export seqtools_subread_PATH=/opt/SeqTools/bin/subread-1.5.2-source/bin
subread-buildindex -o Subreadindex/Subreadindex /mnt/data/variantCallDatabase/iGenomes/Homo_sapiens/UCSC/hg19/Sequence/WholeGenomeFasta/genome.fa
subjunc -T 23  -i Subreadindex/Subreadindex -r SRR902884.fastq -o ABRF-PGM-MSK-A-1/accepted_hits_subjunc.bam

It returns the segmentation fault error message. In additon, below is the detailed log info from subjunc:

As you can see from the progress, the alignment rate decreases dramatically when 70% has been completed. And then it stops when 97% is complete and the segmentation fault error appears. We are also wondering why the rate decreases so rapidly which makes the subjunc aligned not that fast.

Also, we also tested the subjunc aligner on some other datasets, and it works pretty well. So we are questioning if this is particularly related with the data. Could you please look into it? We appreciate your efforts very much.

-Ting
